findings.where: frame 129 of 336, the 'nuzzle' object at x 144-682, y 1566-2082; the same class of object in 01_pulse.png at x 740-960, y 1185-1390 ('hold') and x 990-1230, y 1230-1350 ('nyeh')
findings.what: Three of the thirty-six feelings are smooth untextured 3-D forms rather than objects: the nuzzle clover is one uniform green with a sawtooth polygon margin and no venation, and hold and nyeh are gradient-shaded bodies carrying specular highlights with no material on them.
findings.why: The row forbids stock illustration and 3-D gradient blobs standing in for feeling, and an object with no surface on it is the second of those. Measured: in frame 129, 35.1 per cent of the clover's interior sits below a local standard deviation of 1.0 grey level in a 9-pixel window, against 13.7 per cent for the paper in the same frame and 0.1 per cent for the desk; logs/surfaces.json records obj_clover's tooth at 1.001, the second lowest of the 62 object surfaces it measures. It is three of thirty-six and the rest of the vocabulary is paper, ink and scanned things, which is why this is serious rather than blocking.

findings.where: the RITUALS card at x 370-1075, y 1655-1870 and the ritual row directly beneath it at x 60-1420, y 1880-2000; the same two rows appear in 08_state_propagating.mp4 and 15_authored_feeling.mp4
findings.what: The Rituals surface carries counts: the card reads '3 kept · 53 times · the last yesterday' and the row reads 'sunday 9 call' with '20 times' set against it, so a running number is attached to a recurring act of affection.
findings.why: The brief's failure list names 'any count ... on the Rituals surface'. I am not calling it engagement machinery in substance and not marking it blocking: the numbers are cumulative totals, not consecutive runs, there is no target, no reset, no broken state, no colour change and no prompt to act; the word streak appears nowhere in the 565 literals in logs/strings.json; the same count grammar is used by every other module card on the same screen ('3 ahead', '10 open · 16 done', '3 marked · the next in 66 days', '2 waiting on you · 6 between you'); and in Moments the same event renders as a single tally stroke beside KEPT with no total at all. I read evidence/scenes/03_us.json to check this was not a framing choice: the scene is goTo, wait, shot, so the counts are the app's own. It is still the only score-shaped thing in the set, and the cheapest correction is to drop 'times' from the ritual row and leave 'the last yesterday'.

findings.where: the field stocks_the_paper_had_not_arrived_for, in 10 of the 18 scene reports
findings.what: The build records that in more than half the scenes at least one piece was drawn before its paper stock had loaded, which by the capture's own account paints the app's flat fallback colour under that piece; nothing in the evidence says which piece or whether it was on the glass.
findings.why: A sheet painted a flat colour is exactly the beige rectangle the row forbids, so a record of it happening needs a record of where. Measured: the field is non-empty in 10 of 18 reports (sticky_blue_02 in nine of them, plus graph_03 in 12_search.report.json, and sticky_blue_02_dusk in dusk_pulse.report.json). Nothing flat is visible: my own scan of the ten stills for connected regions below a local standard deviation of 0.5 in a 15-pixel window found the largest, outside the photograph open in 14_media_viewer.png, to be 864 pixels in 04_moments.png, 0.019 per cent of the frame. So this is a latent route to the anti-goal rather than a breach of it, and what is missing is one line per scene naming the piece.

findings.where: the whole middle third, y 1040-2080, and the same surface in 10_first_run.png and behind every note in crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png
findings.what: The desk is the largest surface in the artifact set and it reads as drawn rather than photographed: parallel vertical striations at a constant pitch with two knots rendered as sets of concentric ellipses.
findings.why: I am not scoring this as a breach, because the anti-goal names paper and the desk is wood, and the brief permits a render. It is recorded because it is the surface the eye spends most of its time on and it is nearest the same failure. Measured: bare desk occupies 41.2 per cent of the ten stills by area on average, 69.5 per cent of 10_first_run.png, 61.7 per cent of 13_messenger_states.png and 55.1 per cent of 03_us.png; logs/grain.json puts desk.png's fine_detail_share at 1.83 against its own floor of 1.6 and says in the file that 'a board with only rings on it is a comb'. Its own margin is 0.23.

findings.what: Two of the seventeen artifacts are missing, and 16_setup_android.png is the only place the Android setup copy would have been on the glass, so one of the four anti-goals cannot be checked where it is most exposed.
findings.why: The reason given in evidence/MANIFEST.json and WHY_MISSING.json is a standing fact about the machine rather than a skipped run, and it carries a measurement (no /dev/kvm, adbd answering after 113 minutes with no framework behind it), so I read it as a reason and not an excuse. The exposure is small rather than nil: I read the Android branch of the checklist strings from logs/strings.json instead, app/lib/setup/checklist.dart lines 83 to 115, and found no exclamation mark, no self-naming, no reader addressed as a user, and copy in the same register as the iPhone branch that is on the glass in 17_setup_pwa.png.

what_is_working: No product-marketing voice anywhere I could read. I re-ran eight rules myself over the 565 literals in logs/strings.json rather than trusting its findings list: 0 exclamation marks in rendered text, 0 uses of the word user, 0 self-namings, 0 cheer words (oops, yay, awesome, welcome to, get started, you're all set), 0 engagement words (unlock, earn, reward, achievement, badge, level up, points), 0 emoji, 0 streak words. The six '!' characters in the table are Dart null-assertions inside ${} interpolations and never reach the glass.

The strings on the glass match the table. 10_first_run.png: 'nothing from them yet. the six words are on the other phone.' and 'first one's yours. whatever it is. it only goes to one person.' 05_settings.png: 'quiet from 23:00 until 07:00' over 'wake me / quietly / not at all'. 17_setup_pwa.png: 'this one, the iphone — two phones, one wire between them, nobody else on it.' 03_us.png: 'nothing to do. suspicious.' All lower case, none addressed to a user, none cheerful.
The app never names itself, including in the one string it cannot control the framing of: logs/pwa.json records the installed manifest name as 'the other phone'.

No emoji soup and no colour-emoji glyph anywhere. Measured: 0 pixels above HSV saturation 0.45 with value above 0.35 in eight of the ten stills (01, 02, 03, 05, 10, 12, 13, 17); the only saturated pixels in the whole set are inside two photographs, 0.61 per cent of 04_moments.png and 0.08 per cent of 14_media_viewer.png, and I cropped both to confirm they are birds over a sea and a rendered still life, not glyphs.

The emotional layer is objects and marks, not icons. logs/surfaces.json names 36 feeling objects with an empty 'named_but_neither', and the ones I could see on the glass are a drawn chair, a biro scribble, paper confetti, a folded card, a coffee ring, a paper hat, a paper plane, folded chunks, a rubber-band loop, a staple chain, a crumpled ball and a hand-drawn authored feeling ('tuesday soup', an orange arc drawn with a pen in 15_authored_feeling.mp4).

The feeling names carry no product cheer of their own: crops/haptics_strip.png lists all 36 across six families, and they include 'not okay', 'overwhelmed', 'grey', 'long day', 'snapped' and 'ugh' beside the warm ones, so the vocabulary is not farming affection.

No simulated paper by any of the three routes the row names. No tiled repeating texture: the maximum off-centre autocorrelation of the fibre texture inside the six largest notes of 02_chat.png is 0.411, and every peak sits at a lag of 12 to 16 pixels, which is the ruling and ink period, with no peak at any tile-sized lag. No procedural noise overlay: the maximum absolute normalised cross-correlation between different notes' fibre texture at zero offset is 0.065 over all 15 pairs, so no shared noise field is laid over the sheets. No beige rectangle: the largest connected region below a local standard deviation of 0.5, outside the photograph in 14_media_viewer.png, is 864 pixels, 0.019 per cent of a frame.

The paper survives the zoom. crops/02_chat_300_shadow.png and 02_chat_300_edge.png show individual loose fibres standing off the torn edge and visible tooth across the sheet; crops/02_chat_300_hand.png shows ink with real pressure variance and two differently formed 'i's in one crop. The folded note in 06_unfolding.mp4 at frame 70 keeps its tooth and its fringed tear through the fold rather than flattening to a grey band.

Nothing in the set nags. Notification behaviour is chosen per event type in 05_settings.png as 'wake me / quietly / not at all' with quiet hours, and the pushes in crops/reception.png and reception_state.png read 'noor / wrote something' and 'noor / said how they are' with nothing else in them.

The Rituals event renders as a quiet record where it lands in history: in crops/04_moments_what_happened.png a kept ritual is a single tally stroke beside the word KEPT, with no total, no run and no target.
verdict: The row passes at its floor. Three of the four forbidden interpretations are absent and I could measure their absence rather than assert it: the voice is clean across every string I could read on the glass and every one of the 565 literals in the string table, with zero exclamation marks, zero readers called users and zero self-namings including in the PWA manifest, whose name is 'the other phone'; there is no emoji anywhere, with zero saturated pixels in eight of the ten stills and the only colour in the set sitting inside two photographs; and the paper is not simulated by any of the three routes the row names, with no tiled repeat (max off-centre autocorrelation 0.411, all at the ruling's own period), no shared noise field (max cross-correlation between different sheets 0.065) and no flat fill standing in for a sheet (largest flat region 864 pixels, 0.019 per cent of a frame), while at three hundred per cent the tear still shows loose fibres. What keeps this off ten is the second anti-goal, partially: three of the thirty-six feelings — the nuzzle clover above all, with 35.1 per cent of its interior below a local standard deviation of 1.0 against the paper's 13.7 per cent in the same frame, a uniform green field, a polygon sawtooth margin and no venation — are smooth untextured 3-D forms with specular highlights, which is the 3-D gradient blob the row forbids, dropped into a world where everything else is paper, ink and scanned objects. That is a minority of the vocabulary and correctable object by object, so it is serious rather than blocking. The three minor findings are a count of 'times' on the Rituals surface that is the only score-shaped thing in the set but punishes nothing and can be failed by nobody; a record in ten of eighteen scene reports that a piece was painted with the app's flat fallback colour, with nothing in the evidence saying where, which is a latent route to the very failure the row exists to catch; and the desk, 41.2 per cent of the still set by area, which reads as drawn striations with concentric-ellipse knots and clears its own fine-detail floor by 0.23 — not paper, so not a breach, but the surface nearest the same mistake and the one the eye rests on longest.
not_worth_opening: evidence/crops/06_unfolding_strip.png, 11_chat_scroll_strip.png, 14_media_viewer_strip.png — I stepped the clips' own frames with ffmpeg instead and built my own six- to fourteen-frame samples, which is the same evidence at more points; the media-viewer strip adds nothing my row needs that the still does not carry.

evidence/crops/reception_open.png, reception_allowed.png, reception_replaced.png — the push copy and the notification chrome, which is all my row needs from that scene, is already legible in reception.png and reception_state.png, and I opened reception_picked_up.png for the in-app pocket.

evidence/reliability.json, evidence/coldstart.json, evidence/DIFF.json — transport, messenger and regression evidence. None of it is a surface or a displayed string, so none of the four anti-goals can be present in it.

evidence/logs/haptics.json, haptics.check.json — the felt-distance derivation. My row does not judge whether a pattern is distinguishable; crops/haptics_strip.png gave me the thirty-six names and six families, which is the part that bears on emoji soup and on voice.

evidence/logs/holes.json, lines.json — contact-shadow and baseline-offset measurements. Both are material-truth's row; neither can show a tile, a flat fill or a noise overlay, which are the three things my row's paper clause names.

evidence/logs/scroll_webkit.json, 11_chat_scroll.fling.json, and the per-clip *.frames.json and *.sound.json — frame cost, fling physics, frame distinctness and audio. These decide jank and clip validity, not whether a forbidden interpretation is on screen.

evidence/logs/apk.json, crops.json, reception_scene.json and the per-scene evidence/logs/*.json step records — capture bookkeeping. I read one scene script, evidence/scenes/03_us.json, because I was filing a finding against that artifact and needed to know the counts were not a framing choice; the rest of the framing cannot excuse a string or an object.

evidence/scenes/*.json other than 03_us.json — none of my findings is about what the camera was pointed at, so the framing could not turn any of them into a fault in the picture rather than in the app.
evidence/experiments/what_the_alternates_cost/ — the directory names itself as an experiment rather than an artifact, and it is a scroll-cost comparison, which is not my row.
evidence/.previous/ — the preceding capture. My row asks whether a forbidden interpretation is in this build, which is answered by this capture alone.
evidence/SCORE.json and evidence/critics/<n>/ — another reader's conclusions, closed unopened as the briefing directs.
